parts.label: Understand
parts.title: Make each delivery change earn its release
parts.body:
Set acceptance criteria before changing a prompt, model, tool, or data source. Keep regression cases for known failures and held-out cases for a fresh assessment. A prompt improvement that fixes one example may harm another category. Compare the candidate with the current production version on the same case mix, and review severe failures separately from average gains. For a higher-risk use, add adversarial tests and expert review before a controlled release.

Use a change record that names the component version, expected benefit, affected tasks, test results, owner, and rollback method. A policy update may require a retrieval refresh and citation tests; a new tool can require permissions and final-state tests. Decide which changes can pass a targeted suite and which materially alter the use case and need a full review.

The CAIO should ask whether the evidence supports the proposed exposure. A faster answer does not justify a new data-access failure. If a severe case fails, repair the underlying control and rerun the relevant test family before requesting launch approval.

example.title: A model swap
example.body: A smaller model reduces call cost and passes routine questions, but it omits a material exception in several leave-policy cases. The team retains the production model for that slice, records the failure, and tests a narrower routing strategy rather than shipping the swap everywhere.

exercise.title: Write a change gate
exercise.body: Choose a prompt, model, retrieval, or tool change. Define its expected gain, regression set, new risk cases, quality and cost comparison, severe blocker, approver, rollback method, and next production review.

parts.label: Practice
parts.title: Connect production signals to decisions
parts.body:
A prelaunch set cannot capture every real request. Sample production outcomes with appropriate privacy controls, collect user corrections, and review incidents. Compare observed task categories, languages, regions, and input quality with the evaluation set. If a new category grows, a prior aggregate score can become less representative even though the model has not changed. Keep the feedback path open to frontline staff who see repair work that a satisfaction survey misses.

Define thresholds and actions in advance. A severe privacy incident may trigger immediate disablement and response; a gradual increase in correction rate may trigger a targeted review and new cases. Monitor accepted-task rate, severe errors, latency distribution, cost per accepted task, and manual rework with counts and denominators. Separate changes in traffic mix from changes in performance within a slice.

Give one person authority to pause the feature and another a clear incident communication path. A dashboard that shows a red trend without a named owner and response window does not control the system. The weekly meeting should end with decisions and assigned work.

example.title: A changing case mix
example.body: A support assistant served mostly routine order-status queries during testing. After launch, refund questions grow sharply. Overall success falls. The team reports each task slice, restricts refund handling to draft-only mode, and builds a representative refund set before restoring broader scope.

exercise.title: Build the weekly view
exercise.body: For a hypothetical assistant, specify task success, severe failures, p95 latency, cost per accepted task, correction rate, and traffic mix. Give each a count or denominator, owner, trigger, and action. Include one immediate-stop rule and one investigation rule.

sources: NIST AI RMF Core: ongoing risk management

parts.label: Operate
parts.title: Turn incidents into new evidence
parts.body:
When an AI system causes a material error, first contain the effect and preserve enough trace to understand it under the organisation's privacy and retention rules. Reconstruct the user request, system configuration, source versions, tool calls, final state, and human approvals. Identify whether the problem came from a new task, a bad source, retrieval, generation, a service permission, or an operator handoff. Avoid labelling every failure 'hallucination'; the remedy depends on the stage.

Add a regression case that reproduces the incident, then add nearby variants to test the cause. A single fixed phrase can be memorised. Retest the control in a production-like environment and verify the affected records have been reconciled. Record who authorised restoration and what signal would trigger another pause. If the incident exposed a gap in the original launch claim, revise the permitted scope and assurance record.

Review near misses as well as realised harm. An attempted unauthorised tool call rejected by a service may show that a defence worked, but repeated attempts can reveal a new attack route. Operations, security, legal, and the business owner should share the evidence they need to act.

example.title: A citation incident
example.body: An assistant cites an archived policy and a staff member follows the wrong process. The team corrects the case, removes the archive from retrieval, tests similar effective-date collisions, and checks prior answers for the same source. The restoration decision records the tested index version.

exercise.title: Run an incident review
exercise.body: For a stale-policy answer or duplicate agent write, write the containment action, evidence to preserve, root-cause questions, regression variants, affected-record review, restoration gate, and owner of the revised control.

parts.label: Apply
parts.title: Chair the quality and risk review
parts.body:
Bring a compact packet to a weekly or monthly forum: current scope and versions, task mix, outcomes against baseline, severe failures, human corrections, latency, unit cost, open incidents, and changes awaiting approval. Show trend and counts, not only percentages. Include the worst relevant cases with cause and owner. Keep legal or regulatory claims with the appropriate specialist rather than inferring compliance from a model score.

The forum decides whether to scale, hold, narrow, repair, or retire a capability. Write the decision, evidence, dissent, owner, and review date. If usage is low despite good quality, inspect workflow fit; if usage is high with rising correction work, stop expansion and address quality. A portfolio view can reveal the same failure across products, such as stale document ingestion or weak access filtering.

Board reporting needs the aggregate risk and value story plus exceptions requiring authority or funding. It should not expose personal transcripts. The CAIO's contribution is to connect technical evidence to a business decision and to keep that connection current as the system and users change.

example.title: A two-week decision line
example.body: The quality owner sets an illustrative trigger of any material citation error for immediate review and a drop below 85% accepted among assisted cases for a scope hold. Week 1: 230 assisted of 300 eligible, 210 accepted (91% of assisted), zero material citation errors, p95 latency 9 seconds, $1.90 per accepted case. Week 2: 310 assisted of 420 eligible, 260 accepted (84%), three material citation errors, p95 12 seconds, $2.10 per accepted case. The owner pauses regional expansion and puts affected policy answers into staff review. The index team traces one error to an archived policy, versions a regression case plus date and region variants, rebuilds the index, and must pass those cases and a fresh sample before restoring scope. Finance checks whether higher review effort explains unit cost. Figures and thresholds are teaching assumptions.

exercise.title: Produce the executive packet
exercise.body: Draft a one-page quality review for an illustrative system. Include five measures with denominators, top two failure categories, scope and version, one decision to make, named owner, threshold, and next review date. Explain which facts would justify scaling, pausing, or rollback.
